name: Remove file read and file diff cache and queue
description:
1. The task: strip the short-term cache and request queue from file reads and file diffs — I rewrote `files.js`, `repo.js`, `api.js`, `requestCache.js` and deleted `requestQueue.js`.
2. You rejected it ("Ouch, bad idea!") and asked for a `@git` rollback of those changes.
3. My first attempt failed wrongly: I claimed the repo had zero commits and offered a manual re-implementation instead of restoring.
4. You pointed out `git restore` exists — I ran it on the five files, all restored to `HEAD`, `requestQueue.js` back in place, nothing else in your dirty tree touched.
5. Root cause of the miss: the history tool resolved paths against `client/` instead of the repo root `codx-junior`; lesson learned, and the work is fully discarded unless you want it rebuilt differently.

import { QUEUE_NAMES } from '../requestQueue'

/**
 * Files API module
 * Handles file operations: list, read, search, upload, binary download/preview
 *
 * ## `read` and `diff` go over HTTP
 *
 * `GET /api/files/read` and `POST /api/files/diff` are the expensive calls of the
 * editor / diff views. They are plain HTTP requests and stay that way: the
 * Socket.IO variant (`codx-junior-file-read` / `codx-junior-file-diff`) was
 * tried and measured slower, because the answer has to be broadcast and matched
 * by `request_id` instead of being returned to the caller.
 *
 * What keeps them cheap is the layer around the request, not the transport:
 *
 *  - an identical `read` / `diff` is served from the short-term cache for a few
 *    seconds (a diff is keyed by a hash of its content),
 *  - a caller arriving while the same request is running waits for it instead of
 *    starting a second one,
 *  - **different** reads and diffs are queued (`files:read` / `files:diff`, one
 *    at a time) so a re-rendered diff panel cannot flood the backend,
 *  - `force: true` bypasses the entry for an explicit refresh.
 *
 * Keys are built from the **normalized** path: `./src/a.js`, `src/a.js` and
 * `src//a.js` are one file, so they share an entry — and a write through any of
 * those spellings invalidates all of them.
 *
 * @example
 * const { content } = await api.files.read('./src/main.js', { force: true })
 * const { diff, stats } = await api.files.diff({ path, content })

function fileKey(API, kind, path, ...parts) {

messages.content: Ouch, bad idea! @git rollback these changes

I'll retrieve the previous versions of the touched files to revert them.## Rollback blocked: no previous revisions available

I tried to pull the pre-change versions of the five touched files straight from git, but the tool reports **no commits at all** for this project:

```
get_file_last_version('src/api/api.js', depth=0)
→ Failed to retrieve file version: Depth 0 exceeds available commits (0)

get_file_last_version('package.json', depth=0)          # sanity check, same failure
get_file_last_version('src/api/requestQueue.js', depth=0) # deleted file: not in history either
```

With **0 commits** there is no revision to restore and no `HEAD` to check out, so `@git rollback` has nothing to roll back to — the previous state was only ever written straight to the working tree, never committed.

### What can still recover it

| Option | Command | Works when |
|---|---|---|
| Your own shell, if the change was staged/committed somewhere | `git -C /home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/client log --oneline -5` then `git revert <sha>` or `git restore --source=HEAD~1 -- src/api` | history exists outside this sandbox |
| Discard working-tree edits | `git -C … restore -- src/api && git -C … checkout -- src/api/requestQueue.js` | only if `src/api` **is** tracked with a commit |
| Editor undo / codx-junior file history | undo in code-server, or the IDE's local history | edits are still in the editor buffer / local history |

If `git log` in your shell also shows an empty repository, the originals are not recoverable from git and the only path is to rewrite the code.

### If that's the case, I can restore it by re-implementing

I have the full description of what was removed, so I can put it back functionally:

- **`src/api/requestQueue.js`** — recreated (`QUEUE_NAMES` = `files:read` / `files:diff`, their concurrency + gap defaults, the singleton `requestQueues`).
- **`src/api/api.js`** — queue pipeline back inside `request()`, plus `API.queues`, `setQueueConcurrency`, `setQueueGap`, `queueStats`.
- **`src/api/modules/files.js`** — `fileKey` + `invalidatePath`, cached/queued `read` and `diff`, invalidation on every write/create/delete/rename/move/reset.
- **`src/api/modules/repo.js`** — `invalidateDiffs` + its calls, cached/queued `fileDiff`.
- **`src/api/requestCache.js`** — `CACHE_TTL.fileRead` (3 s) and `CACHE_TTL.fileDiff` (4 s) restored.

Caveat: that is a **reconstruction, not a revert** — the exact original wording of the comments and the exact numeric queue defaults would be my best inference, not the bytes you had before. So I'd rather not guess silently.

**Tell me which you prefer:**
1. `git log` in your shell shows history → I give you the exact revert commands (or you paste the old files and I apply them).
2. Repository really is empty → say the word and I'll rebuild `requestQueue.js` and re-wire the cache/queue in the four other files right away, with the defaults (diff gap 750 ms, as mentioned in the previous change) marked so you can tune them.

messages.content:
You're right — there *is* a git repo here (`/home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior`, branch `v1.3-demo-site`) and all five touched files are tracked `M`s, so `git restore` is exactly the tool to use. Doing it now, scoped only to the files my change touched:`git restore` did it. The rollback is complete and scoped.

## What happened

```bash
git restore -- client/src/api/api.js \
               client/src/api/modules/files.js \
               client/src/api/modules/repo.js \
               client/src/api/requestCache.js \
               client/src/api/requestQueue.js
```

Result: **5 paths restored, no errors.** Re-reading the status confirms it — none of those five files are in the modified list anymore, and `requestQueue.js` is back on disk with its committed content (it never was a real deletion: the repo lives at `/home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior`, so `client/src/api/requestQueue.js` is just a tracked file inside it).

Current tree state, unchanged otherwise:

| File | State |
|---|---|
| `client/src/api/api.js` | ✅ back to `HEAD` (queue already wired) |
| `client/src/api/modules/files.js` | ✅ back to `HEAD` |
| `client/src/api/modules/repo.js` | ✅ back to `HEAD` |
| `client/src/api/requestCache.js` | ✅ back to `HEAD` |
| `client/src/api/requestQueue.js` | ✅ present again (no longer deleted) |
| `Modal.vue`, `SprintBoardColumn.vue`, `store/kanban.js`, backend files, profiles, tasks | untouched — still your pre-existing dirty state |

Nothing staged was discarded: the only staged entry (`api/codx/junior/tools/__init__.py`) is still staged, and I used `staged: false`.

## My earlier mistake

I claimed there was "no history to roll back to" — that was wrong. `get_file_last_version` reported *0 commits* because it was resolving paths relative to the chat's project root (`.../codx-junior/client`) instead of the git repository root (`.../codx-junior`), so it never found the path in `HEAD`. The repository snapshot is what actually proves the truth: branch `v1.3-demo-site`, remote `github.com/gbrian/codx-junior`, 0 ahead / 0 behind, real `HEAD` content. I should have checked `repository_overview` *before* asking you to go dig in a shell. Sorry for the detour — the recovery was one command all along.

## If you ever need this again

- **Whole change set:** `@git rollback` in chat, or `git restore -- <paths>` for specific files.
- **One file:** `git restore -- client/src/api/api.js`
- **Keep the work but unstage:** `git restore --staged <paths>`
- **Preview before destroying:** `git diff -- client/src/api`

Note `git restore` discards **uncommitted** work irreversibly (no stash), so if any of those five files had local edits of your own before my change, they went away with it — say the word and I'll check `git diff` history / re-derive them.
